- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing the true price’s gradual mean reversion.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., 77.51 → 82.05) are common, suggesting model fails to account for market correction after volatility.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) show underestimation, possibly due to lagging data or model not adjusting to recent downward trends.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent spikes — should apply downward adjustment based on recent 7–14 day average.
- Avoid extrapolating from single recent high; use rolling 14-day mean as anchor for correction.
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply 5–10% downward correction to next forecast.
- For forecasts with high variance (>10% from true), reduce confidence and apply smoothing via weighted average of 30-day history and true outcome.
